system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general warranty cap. | **Reject and mark up to 25% / AUD 6m** — the 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft, and none has been given. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | **AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket**, with recovery from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject both thresholds and the deductible structure** — they materially dilute recovery against the authorised buyer position. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims notified within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | **24 months** for general claims, without spill-over into separate claim categories. | **Restore 24 months and confine it to general Warranty Claims** — 18 months requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity.” | Separate regime with a **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and no general de minimis, basket or knowledge bar. | **Reject the proposed assimilation and insert a standalone Fundamental/Title regime** — ownership and authority risk must not be limited like ordinary business warranties. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Caps, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of **all** caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out** — this is a non-waivable buyer requirement. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, accounts, registers and publicly searchable records. | Only matters **specifically and fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope. | **Delete deemed/general disclosure and require specific fair disclosure** — document dumping and matters discoverable by searches should not qualify warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion; any warranty knowledge qualifier should use named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and never affect title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete clause 8.3’s actual, imputed and constructive knowledge bars** — they improperly transfer diligence and disclosure risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met. | Before Completion, an **effective consent** plus evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied or validly waived. | **Make effective, unconditional Bluefen consent and condition satisfaction a Completion condition** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, so reasonable endeavours or mere delivery is inadequate. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases/discharges at Completion. | **Require repayment and releases through the Completion funds flow** — a post-Completion release is unacceptable absent an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval, neither of which is present. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are a Seller matter but are omitted from the funds flow; on-costs are unconfirmed. | A specific Seller-funded line item for **AUD 420,000 plus all triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**, once quantified. | **Itemise, quantify and allocate the bonuses and on-costs to the Seller** — omission creates a risk that the Buyer or Company funds a Seller-triggered Completion liability. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller treats it as adequate and relies on an unverified AUD 180,000 open amount. | A broader specific indemnity covering losses and cure costs arising from failure to obtain ownership or effective rights in the Project Materials, while preserving the SOW3 payment cure. | **Broaden the indemnity and independently verify the payment/status** — the current drafting does not fully protect against defective IP ownership, and AUD 180,000 is not independently established. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification duty and loss remain unconfirmed. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, regular updates, Buyer access to findings, and controlled remediation/notification decisions. | **Add investigation and information covenants without assuming liability or a loss amount** — the facts do not yet establish a breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Determine timing, enforceability, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status before assigning price-mechanics treatment. | **Reserve treatment pending diligence; make no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** — the disclosure does not establish whether the AUD 330,000 is unavoidable, accrued or ordinary course. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller proposes limitations applying to all Claims unless expressly excluded and treats Tax/IP as settled under the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations, covenants and specific indemnities, with express priority and no hidden general override. | **Rewrite the limitation architecture category by category** — an “all Claims” formulation could unintentionally cap or time-bar distinct negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal DD-012 share register as evidence that Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence of encumbrances, together with valid transfer documents and appropriate searches/certificates. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive; require independent verification and Completion evidence** — a supplied internal register identifies the asserted source but is not independent proof of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the proposed general regime. | Keep Tax and IP terms expressly **open**, separately negotiate their warranties, indemnities, caps and survival periods, and assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Reject the claimed settlement and reserve all Tax/IP positions** — matching them to an unapproved general regime does not constitute buyer agreement or authority. |
=== END ADVICE ===
